content.comment_body: After upgrading our portable computers to newer models, especially those running Windows 10 Pro, we can no longer access the remote device using the [product_name] program. We have attached the error message received. Can anyone explain what might be causing this issue?

Hello, Are your PC and [product_name] module on the same network subnet? If so, consider temporarily disabling your PC's antivirus and firewall. Additionally, for newly purchased [product_name] modules, the latest software version may be required to ensure communication.

If you have a [product_name] with article number [article_no], you need [product_name] software version [version_no]. Older versions of [product_name] software won't connect to newer [product_name] modules.

I encountered a similar issue with Windows 10. Ensuring both devices were on the same subnet didn't solve it. Reinstalling drivers from the CD failed as well, but after installing the driver recommended by [user_name], it worked. [url] [url]
Just to clarify, your scenario uses a [product_name] with its specific cable, while the thread starter has a [product_name] utilizing an ethernet connection.
Thanks for pointing that out—I was dealing with two different [product_name] devices, with separate article numbers [article_no] and [article_no].

I received [product_name] software version [version_no] recently, and use the corresponding [product_name] hardware. Communication was fine two days ago, but now it's impossible. Tried all usual fixes with Windows 10 Pro, firewall disabled, antivirus off, restarting hardware and PC, but nothing works. The error is identical to one posted by another user. Would appreciate assistance!
Are you using a router with DHCP enabled, and is the [product_name] device's IP within the DHCP range?

Thanks for suggesting that. I've loaded a test program on the [product_name] module recently with no passwords set. The [product_name] and [product_name] communication module are on the same network switch, and the PC connects through it as well. My PC is at 192.168.0.1, [product_name] at 192.168.0.2, and the communication module at 192.168.0.3 (all subnets 255.255.255.0). I can access [product_name] data via the web management interface, but need to upload a complete program. Since both devices communicate over the switch, I doubt the switch is the issue. It seems something with [product_name] software is the problem, but I'm unsure what. The software does show the device at the correct IP.

I tried changing addresses and factory resetting the module, but the result is the same: the main module communicates with the communication module, and the communication module communicates with the PC, but the software detects the module and still can't communicate with it. There are no other devices on the switch. Running out of ideas—can anyone help? Update: Problem solved. The module can't communicate with both the communication module and the PC at once; to connect with the PC, the communication module needs to be in a safe status. Thanks to everyone.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants face ongoing connectivity problems between their Windows 10 Pro PCs and [company_name] [product_name] modules when using the relevant software. While some resolved the issue with driver or software updates, others still encounter difficulties even after extensive troubleshooting. The issues are most pronounced with newer hardware and matching software versions. Proper network configuration and device detection are consistent challenges, especially when multiple devices share the same subnet.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect consistent and easy connectivity with clear device recognition between Windows 10 Pro computers and [company_name] [product_name] hardware, regardless of hardware or software updates, without requiring advanced troubleshooting.
